name: Boma–Badingilo Migratory Landscape
subtitle: A natural property on the UNESCO World Heritage List since 2026.

facts.label: In Danger
facts.value: on UNESCO's List of World Heritage in Danger (since 2026)

parts.text: UNESCO describes the property in these words: “The property comprises Boma National Park, Badingilo National Park, and the surrounding floodplain and savanna landscapes in South Sudan. Located at the interface between the Sudd wetland system and the East Sudanian Savanna, it encompasses an extensive mosaic of seasonally flooded grasslands, wetlands, floodplains, woodlands, and savannas shaped by seasonal rainfall and flood dynamics. These interconnected ecosystems sustain one of the world’s largest remaining terrestrial mammal migrations, with an estimated six million White-eared Kob, Tiang, and Mongalla Gazelle moving across a vast and largely unimpeded landscape in response to changing environmental conditions. The site also reflects important cultural, and linguistic diversity of the region with the Murle, Dinka, Nuer, Anyuak and Toposa and other ethnic groups who have been custodians of this landscape through herding, farming and fishing for centuries and even millennia. The property also supports important populations of numerous large mammal species, including Nile Lechwe, African Savanna Elephant, African Wild Dog, Lion, Leopard, Northeastern Africa Cheetah, and Beisa Oryx, as well as significant assemblages of waterbirds, raptors, and migratory bird species. Its exceptional scale, ecological connectivity, habitat diversity, and relative intactness sustain ecological and biological processes that have become increasingly rare globally.”
Boma National Park is in eastern South Sudan near the Ethiopian border. Wikipedia says it was established in 1977 and covers 22,800 km² of grasslands and floodplains.

The article describes the world's largest annual animal migration, the Great Nile Migration Landscape, in which antelope such as Bohor reedbuck, tiang and white-eared kob move between Bandingilo and Boma National Parks.

It says African Parks signed a 10-year renewable agreement with the government of South Sudan in August 2022 to restore the two parks, and that in July 2026 UNESCO designated the Boma–Badingilo Migratory Landscape and listed it as endangered.
